questions.question: Why strings are of reference type in C#.NET?

options.text: To reduce the overall memory for strings

questions.explanation: In C#, strings are immutable which means that once a string object is created, its value cannot be changed. By making strings as reference types, C# allows the same string object to be used by multiple variables which reduces the memory footprint for strings. So, strings are created on heap and a reference is passed to the program.
